Pudu outlines shared AI architecture across robot forms

Its European partner summit introduced a strategy built around PuduFM and PuduAgent OS.

RoboticsTomorrow / Pudu Robotics ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

A shared technology strategy

Pudu Robotics outlined its One Brain, Multiple Embodiments strategy at its first European Partner Summit in Amsterdam, according to its November 5 announcement. It brings delivery, cleaning, industrial transport, embodied AI, commercial mowing and home lawn-care lines under a shared technological framework.

Reusable software, task-specific hardware

PuduFM and PuduAgent OS are intended to share AI capabilities, software modules and skills across platforms, while hardware and motion control remain task-specific. Pudu aims to shorten development and deployment cycles, but the release does not provide a quantified comparative cost study.

Market context and limits

Pudu reports operations in over 20 European countries and average regional annual revenue growth above 60% over the past two years. The news is the shared strategy and portfolio presentation. It does not mean every exhibited robot is new or every skill already transfers without adaptation.
